Rain forms through a simple cycle involving water, heat, and air. First, the sun heats up water in oceans, lakes, and rivers. This heat turns the liquid water into invisible gas called water vapor, which rises into the sky. This process is called evaporation.

As the warm vapor goes higher, the air becomes cooler. The cool air causes the water vapor to turn back into tiny liquid droplets. These droplets gather around small particles like dust or smoke to form clouds. This step is called condensation.

When many tiny droplets join together in a cloud, they become too heavy to stay floating in the air
